title: I can't start RPG maker MV

posts.author: NickTheBrick
posts.body:
It started to not open just today, despite the fact that is opened just fine two days ago.
I did many things that were recommended for this type of issue, like making sure my drivers were up to date, opening as administrator, turning off my antivirus and firewall, but none of them worked. I am currently on Windows 10, and I know that it's no longer supported, would I need to update to windows 11 then to fix this issue, I am hoping not.
Please someone help!

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body:
For what it's worth, I'm able to open it on Windows 10 without issue, so I don't expect the fix to involve upgrading to Windows 11. That said, I don't have any idea what the fix
would
be, unfortunately. It would also probably help to know whether you are using the Steam version or the standalone version.

posts.body:

Click to expand...
I don't understand, I use MV and MZ normally on Windows 8.1 and I used MV on 10 just this week.
RMMV and MZ have not received recent updates, so I can only understand that you interpreted this as the end of Microsoft support, this does not mean that Windows will simply stop.
The problem probably occurs when the user installs or receives updates to some other third-party software that affects the normal functioning of Windows.

posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: Yeah, to be clear, the only thing that "Windows 10 is not supported" means is that you can't update your Windows anymore. That doesn't mean any of your programs would stop working.

Okay, that makes a little harder to diagnose. Here are 2 more options to try:
Go to your Steam library, right click on the game and choose Properties > Installed Files and then click on Verify Integrity of Game Files
You can also try clearing your Steam download cache. Open Steam, click on Steam > Settings > Downloads and then on Clear Cache. You will have to log back into Steam after this.
If these don't work, has there been anything new added to your computer lately? Have you downloaded any new apps, games, programs, etc? Has your anti-virus been updated recently before this issue happened? Can you think of anything else that may have changed?

I doubt you need Windows 11, but I use it and it's great so you can just for that. But it sounds like an issue talking to Steam to tell it you own the game. That's what happens when you copy a game and try to play it outside of a Steam account. The game will start and then fail. So it sounds like an issue with Steam and I would talk to their support. If for any reason the App ID is not lining up with your purchase, this is exactly what happens. Most likely it's a glitch in the store that somehow removed the fact you purchased it. The fact you have uninstalled and reinstalled it says it's not in the program itself, but on Steam's side of things.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Just FYI, as it works now:
1)
updating the driver is not only suggested for the version, but for repairing damaged drivers.
This is especially true if the program worked before.
So don't trust Windows if the autoupdater claims to already have the best driver, always download the driver setup of the manufacturer and force its installation with the setup.
2)
that behaviour can also happen if a protection program gets a false positive and stops the program before the suspected virus can harm the computer.
you should check your AV settings.
